text:
maria: Quick note — our services keep re-implementing client-side rate heuristics. The python SDK doesn't expose a battle-tested async throttle helper that understands Retry-After + quota headers (x-rw-quota-*, X-RateLimit-*). Should we add one?

jia: We should. We have a prototype in eng-ml but it isn't public. What are the minimal guarantees you need? Non-blocking for asyncio, predictable behavior on 429 and Retry-After?

maria: Exactly. Want an opt-in AsyncThrottleMiddleware that: honors Retry-After if present, falls back to header-derived quotas, uses a token-bucket with small jitter, and provides test hooks for time. Avoid long-lived background tasks unless the user opts in.

anita: Strong +1 for typed helpers. Everyone's copying the parse logic. If we export parse_quota_header -> QuotaInfo (dataclass/NamedTuple) with clear semantics it will help mypy users. Docstrings should show integer seconds, float seconds ("0.5"), and HTTP-date parsing for Retry-After.

trevor: Sketch for API (pseudo):

@dataclass
class QuotaInfo:
    limit: int
    remaining: int
    reset_at: float  # unix timestamp

def parse_quota_headers(headers: Mapping[str, str]) -> Optional[QuotaInfo]:
    """Support X-RateLimit-*/x-rw-quota-* and Retry-After parsing (int/float/HTTP-date)."""

Also middleware usage:

client = AsyncClient(...)
client.add_middleware(AsyncThrottle(
    max_burst=200,
    window=60,
    refill_rate=200/60,
    backoff_policy=exp_jitter(base=0.2, cap=4.0)
))

client-bot: ci-bot: opened PR draft #2045 and issue #912 for SDK async throttle.

jia: Nice. A few implementation notes from previous bugs:
- Parse Retry-After before decrementing local token to avoid races when one request sees Retry-After and other in-flight requests still count down.
- Allow middleware to be configured in "optimistic" mode (best-effort without blocking) and "strict" mode (await when tokens exhausted).
- Tests should simulate header races and sub-second Retry-After values.

anita: Agreed. I'll add unit tests for: header parsing, HTTP-date formats, float seconds, concurrent requests where one header sets Retry-After, and behavior when header values are missing. Also export small helpers to inject fake_time for deterministic testing.

maria: API ergonomics: prefer small surface area. parse_quota_headers + AsyncThrottle class + a tiny examples page in the docs under "client/concurrency" showing common patterns (background workers, web request handlers).

trevor: Edge-case: some proxies fold header names or uppercase them. parse helper should be case-insensitive and accept both hyphenated and camel variants — normalize keys.

jia: Good catch. Also mention that Retry-After could be huge; cap backoff to a configured maximum to avoid waiting days.

client-bot: ci-bot: linked PR draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/pull/2045, issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-sdk/issues/912

maria: I'll prototype our service's variant into the SDK PR once tests land. Thanks all :heart:
